title: Grateful Dead Live at DuPont Gym - MIT on 1970-05-07
source: this is a remaster of shnid 5439

ai_review.summary: A solid audience tape that captures a relaxed MIT show, highlighted by an epic Love Light medley and strong renditions of Candyman, Easy Wind and The Other One.
ai_review.review: The recording, improved by SirMick’s restoration work, offers decent clarity for a 1970 audience source with occasional hiss, chat‑on‑mic moments and pitch quirks during the Love Light suite. Musically the show is praised for its laid‑back vibe, long acoustic set and especially the extended Love Light jam that weaves St. Stephen, Darkness and China Cat themes, plus standout performances of Candyman, Easy Wind, Good Lovin' and The Other One.

ai_rating.rationale: Across 12 reviews the average rating is ~3.3 stars; most reviewers praise the performance and deem the audio decent for its era, while a few note technical annoyances (chat, pitch issues) and track‑splitting complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear for an early‑70s audience tape; SirMick’s cleanup reduces hiss and improves instrument balance. Some reviewers note occasional chat on the mic, minor drop‑outs, pitch fluctuations (especially in the Love Light suite) and a few glitches in the first set.

standout_songs: Love Light (with St. Stephen, Darkness & China Cat jams)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑set marathon with a very long acoustic portion, high audience energy and a relaxed vibe. The Love Light medley serves as the centerpiece of the second set; occasional chat interrupts but overall the pacing is steady and enjoyable despite some first‑set slowness.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s banter (e.g., the ‘Eleven’ joke) adds humor; his lead work shines in the extended jams of Love Light, Easy Wind and The Other One.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s rhythmic cues (“beats on Beat It On Down the Line”, Alligator calls) are noted as solid and drive the high‑energy sections.
